Unofficial until approved by the
  Alhambra City Council
  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  May 13, 2024
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:06 p.m., on Monday, May 13, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in the Council
Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Interim Director of Public Works/Utilities Ahlen, Director of Finance Lieu,
Director of Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Fire Chief Ragusa, Police
Chief Kennedy, Senior Planner Siva

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maza

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIALS

1.  PROCLAMATIONS – F2M24-3

  A.  The Alhambra City Councill ratified the action of Mayor Maza in proclaiming May 2024
  as Asian American Native Hawaiian Pacific Islander Heritage Month in Alhambra.

  B.  The Alhambra City Council ratified the action of Mayor Maza in proclaiming June 2024
  as LGBTQ+ Pride Month in Alhambra.

MAZA: Mayor Maza requested to move on to Item No. 4 before the public hearings and Council
agreed.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

2.  PUBLIC WORKS MAINTENANCE & IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025
  RENEWAL – F2M24-44, N2M24-55, R2M24-15

  Interim Director of Public Works & Utilities AHLEN delivered a staff report. This was the time
  and place set by Notice No. N2M24-55 for the City Council to hold a public hearing to consider
  the following:

2-12-24  1
   A.  The Public Works Maintenance and Improvement District No. 1 - Zone A includes the
  downtown area only and was established to provide a source of funding to operate and
  maintain specialized improvements. Those improvements include items such as decorative
  sidewalk planters, landscape medians, decorative sidewalk and paving and the
  Washington Twin streetlights. This assessment was proposed to be unchanged from the
  2023-24 level; and,

  B.  The Public Works Maintenance and Improvement District No. 1 - Zone B was established
  to fund debt service on a bond issue and ongoing maintenance and operation of the City-
  wide street lights, sidewalks, curb and gutters, streets, street trees, median landscaping
  and municipal parking lots and structures. The work is performed by a combination of a
  concrete crew, a two-person electrical crew (who also maintain traffic signals), an asphalt
  crew, and contractors. This assessment was proposed to be unchanged from the 2023-24
  level; and,

  C.  The Public Works Maintenance and Improvement District No. 1 - Zone C was established
  in 1987 and includes generally those properties located on both sides of Main Street,
  between Atlantic and Palm, and on both sides of Palm, between Main and Commonwealth.
  The purpose of Zone C is to provide funding for the ongoing maintenance and operation of
  the public improvements, which were constructed in the Auto Row area and include the
  grass parkway, the feature lights between Atlantic and Olive, and the street trees. This
  assessment was proposed to be unchanged from the 2023-24 level.

  Opened & Closed Public Hearing: Mayor MAZA opened the public hearing and, as there
  was no one present that wished to speak, closed the same.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. AHLEN discussed repair and
  maintenance schedules, avenues for public reporting of sites which need repairs, and
  emergency repairs for in response to street light maintenance. Mayor MAZA also discussed
  street light outages and emergency repairs.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-15 entitled:  A
  Resolution of the Alhambra City Council ordering the renewal of the City of Alhambra Public
  Works Maintenance and Improvements District No. 1 for Fiscal Year 2024-2025, confirming
  the Assessment Diagram and Assessment therefor and providing for the Assessment Levy in
  connection therewith

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  PÉREZ, MALONEY, LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

3.  2024-2025 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN FOR CDBG AND HOME PROGRAMS – F2M24-48,
  N2M24-51, M2M24-85

  Assistant City Manager GARCIA delivered a staff report and Erin LAY, with Veronica Tam &
  Associates delivered a report. This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M24-51 for
  the City Council to hold a public hearing to consider the proposed Community Development
  Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME funding for the City of Alhambra’s proposed 2024-2025
  Annual Action Plan and to receive comment pursuant to and in compliance with the Federal
  Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) pre-submission requirements. For FY
  2024-25, while HUD had not officially notified the City of its funding allocations, pursuant CPD
  Notice 24-01, the City could proceed with the hearing of its Action Plan using an estimated
  funding amount based on the FY 2023-24 CDBG and HOME allocations. The City would delay
  the submission of the FY 2024-25 Action Plan in the Integrated Disbursement and Information
  2
5-13-24
   System (IDIS) until the FY 2024-25 CDBG and HOME allocations were announced by HUD.
  The City of Alhambra estimated it would receive $847,164 in CDBG entitlement funds and
  have available $464,149 in unallocated prior year funds for a total of $1,311,313 from CDBG.
  The City also expected to receive $569,982 in HOME funds. If the actual FY 2024-25
  allocations for CDBG of HOME were greater or less than the estimates used, the amount for
  each project would be increased or decreased at the same percentage, with the Admin, CHDO
  Reserve, and Public Services amounts (as applicable) rounded down to the nearest dollar to
  remain under the funding caps. The following programs were proposed to be funded from
  CDBG and HOME during FY 2024-25:

  Proposed Work Program (CDBG)
  Administration  $144,432
  Fair Housing Services  $25,000
  Code Enforcement  $200,000
  Senior Case Mgmnt (Public Services)  $127,074
  Home Improvement (Minor)  $350,658
  Subtotal  $847,164
  ADA Ramps Citywide (Prior Year Funds)  $464,149
  Total CDBG  $1,311,313

  Proposed Work Program (HOME)
  Administration  $56,998
  CHDO (New Construction)  $85,497
  Home Improvement (Major)  $427,487
  Total HOME  $569,982

  The HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee reviewed the one-year Action Plan as presented at
  the May 7, 2024 Regular Meeting of the HCDA Advisory Committee. The notice for this hearing
  and the 30-day public review of the 2024-25 Annual Action Plan was published in the
  Pasadena Star News, La Opinion, and World Journal newspapers. The plan was also available
  for review at City Hall and on the City's website. As of the date of drafting this report, no public
  comments were received.

  Ms. LAY reported on the formal notice received from HUD and the 24-25 Entitlement
  Allocation. The revised amounts were as follows: $834,539.00 from CDBG; $440,224.00 from
  HOME. The proposed programs were adjusted as follows:

  Proposed Work Program (CDBG)
  Administration  $141,908
  Fair Housing Services  $25,000
  Senior Case Mgmnt (Public Services)  $125,181
  Code Enforcement  $200,000

  Proposed Work Program (HOME)
  Administration  $44,022
  CHDO (New Construction)  $66,034
  Home Improvement (Major)  $330,168

  Opened Public Hearing: Mayor MAZA opened the public hearing.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova, spoke regarding the HCDA
  Citizen Advisory Committee meeting, the revisions made to the documents, the
  recommendation of the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee, the loss of HOME funds, and
  proposed budget adjustments for the next 5-year plan.

  3
5-13-24
   Closed Public Hearing: After receiving public comment, Mayor MAZA closed the public
  hearing.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor PÉREZ and Ms. GARCIA discussed public feedback regarding
  assistance from the Housing Rights Center, the potential of hiring a Fair Housing Services
  Case Management, and concerns regarding the Housing Rights Center’s response time.
  Councilmember MALONEY supported the document and proposed that additional changes
  could be reviewed during the adoption of the new 5-year plan. Councilmember LEE and Ms.
  GARCIA. discussed the new construction CHDO program, affordable units for moderate
  income renters and the response time from the Housing Rights Center. Councilmember
  ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. GARCIA discussed additional services or outreach through
  the Alhambra Civic Center Library, changes made by the Housing Rights Center, the Citywide
  ADA Ramps program, the Senior Case Management program and the excellent job of the
  current Senior Case Management team. Mayor MAZA expressed gratitude to staff for their
  work on the document. Mr. MALONEY and Ms. GARCIA confirmed the updated allocation
  numbers.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the proposed 2024-2025 Annual Action Plan for
  the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME programs and authorized staff
  to submit the plan to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). (
  M2M24-85)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATIONS

4.  CHAMBER OF COMMERCE UPDATE – F2M21-43

  Alhambra Chamber of Commerce President, Mr. John BWARIE, presented an update for
  Chamber of Commerce activities from January 2024 to March 2024. Topics included recent
  events, outreach to new businesses, raising awareness of local businesses for employees at
  large companies in Alhambra, and volunteer opportunities for non-profit work.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. BWARIE discussed attempts
  to attract new businesses to Valley Blvd. and Fremont Ave. Councilmember LEE and Mr.
  BWARIE discussed the pilot program, the challenges of continuing new businesses, and
  recent robbery and retail theft trends. Vice Mayor PÉREZ and Mr. BWARIE discussed vacant
  businesses particularly those left by the closure of large box stores and the possibility of a
  vacancy tax on property owners for chronically vacant locations. Mayor MAZA echoed the
  comments and concerns of his fellow councilmembers and expressed hope that the new
  zoning code update would help attract new businesses.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and ordered filed this informational report.

5.  AMENDED BUDGET REVIEW AND RESOLUTION ADOPTING FY 2023-24 AND FY 2024-
  25 BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS – F2M23-17, R2M24-20

  On June 26, 2023, the City Council adopted the Fiscal Years 2023-24 and 2024-25 Budget.
  Director of Finance LIEU presented an Amended Budget Review to update the City’s financial
  projections and appropriations for both fiscal years. The presentation is on file in the City
  4
5-13-24
   Clerk’s office. During the fiscal year, unforeseen financial needs and opportunities typically
  arise, which require City Council approval of recommended adjustments to projected revenues
  and expenditures. Staff presented an Amended General Fund Budget with slight
  unappropriated surpluses for both fiscal years due to one time savings from grants and billings.
  Historically, these surpluses have been allocated towards important needs such as reserve
  funds, capital repair and replacement, pension and retirement obligations, and acquisition of
  necessary equipment. Appropriations from these surpluses are typically made through
  Council-approved budget adjustments.

  Discussion:  Council expressed gratitude to staff for their work. Councilmember
  MALONEY and Ms. LIEU discussed the General Fund emergency balance as well as the
  pension liability balance. Councilmember LEE and Ms. LIEU also discussed the unfunded
  pension liability and the retirement programs through CALPERS. Councilmember
  ANDRADE-STADLER thanked staff and Council for their pursuit of grant funding for projects.
  Mayor MAZA also praised staff for their pursuit of grant funding and the increases to the
  emergency fund.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the Amended Budget Review for Fiscal
  Year 2023-24 and 2024-25 and related reports; and, adopted Resolution No. R2M24-20
  entitled: A Resolution of the Alhambra City Council adopting Fiscal Years 2023-24 and 2024-
  25 Budget adjustments of the City of Alhambra, Golf Course Clubhouse Corporation, Alhambra
  Capital Improvements Corporation, Alhambra Parking Authority, Alhambra Facilities Financing
  Authority and the Alhambra Public Financing Authority adopting the Fiscal Year 2023-24 and
  2024-25 budget adjustments.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  PÉREZ
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  HISTORIC PRESERVATION PROGRAM SURVEY UPDATE (PHASE 2) – F2M20-51

  Senior Planner SIVA delivered a staff report, Alexandra PERLMAN and Kari FOWLER, from
  Historic Resources Group (HRG), and Evanne ST. CHARLES and Mary RINGHOFF with
  Architectural Resources Group, delivered a presentation. The presentation is on file in the City
  Clerk’s office. In response to City Council’s Strategic Plan item to undertake the preservation
  of notable structures and following a series of community outreach and workshops, on July
  13, 2020, staff presented a historic preservation program to the City Council that included the
  preparation of a Historic Context Statement (Phase 1); a survey of potentially historic
  properties (Phase 2); and development of a Historic Preservation Ordinance (Phase 3). Phase
  1 was completed in March 2022, and on September 26, 2022, the City Council awarded a
  contract to Historic Resources Group (HRG) for Phases 2 and 3 of the Historic Preservation
  Program. HRG now completed Phase 2, the survey of potentially historic properties. The
  historic resources survey built on the work started during Phase 1 of the project and provided
  a solid baseline of information about the built environment in Alhambra in order to begin
  working with the City and the community on the development of a potential historic
  preservation ordinance under Phase 3. The historic resources survey represented the first
  comprehensive citywide survey undertaken in Alhambra. The period of study for this project
  dated from the development of Alhambra’s earliest extant resources in the late 19th century
  through 1980. No potential historic resources were formally designated as part of this survey.
  Under Phase 3 of the project, community meetings would be held for each City Council district
  followed by targeted outreach to all individual properties listed in the survey to collect feedback
  and input on the development of the Historic Preservation Ordinance, which was anticipated
  to be presented to the City Council for adoption in Spring 2025.
  5
5-13-24
   The Historic Resources Survey Report was posted and available for public review here:
  https://historicalhambra.squarespace.com/documents

  Public Comment:
  1) Bert NG, 203 S. Cordova St., spoke regarding the changes he has witnessed in the City, his
  excitement with the potential Historic Preservation Ordinance, and urged Council to implement
  temporary protections for historic homes during the preliminary phases of the Historic
  Preservation Ordinance.

  2) Jennifer NG, S. Cordova St., thanked Council and staff for working with the homeowners in her
  neighborhood to establish their historic status. She also urged Council to implement interim
  protections for historic homes during the preliminary phases of the Historic Preservation
  Ordinance.

  3) Melissa MICHELSON suggested that the Historic Preservation Commission could take on
  additional work for the Historic Preservation Ordinance.

  4) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., commended the consultants for their work, echoed
  Mr. and Ms. Ng’s requests for interim protections, and discussed affordable housing sources.

  Discussion:  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Director of Community
  Development HO discussed the notification of property owners of their home’s historic status
  and the Historic Preservation Commission. Councilmember LEE and City Manager
  BINNQUIST discussed the possibility of speeding up the approval process to address ongoing
  building permits submitted for buildings which might be covered by the ordinance once it is
  approved, the timeline of public outreach in each district as well as citywide outreach, and
  compiling public input for the Historic Preservation Commission to use in drafting the
  ordinance. Ms. LEE further discussed the involvement of the Historic Preservation
  Commission and their role in connection with the Planning Commission. Councilmember
  MALONEY, Mr. HO, and City Attorney MONTES continued to discuss interim protections for
  potentially historic homes and the outreach to property owners. Mr. MALONEY and Ms.
  BINNQUIST continued to discuss public outreach or review during the interim period before
  approval.

  Vice Mayor PÉREZ agreed with Ms. Binnquist’s suggestion that staff seek input on a draft
  Historic Preservation Ordinance rather than seeking input before a draft could be written. She
  further discussed outreach and education for the public. Ms. PÉREZ and Mr. HO discussed
  individually eligible resources, smaller historic districts, developing the work program for the
  Historic Preservation Commission, and the next phases of the project. Ms. PÉREZ and Ms.
  FOWLER discussed the next public outreach phases, the community meetings, and the
  timeline for the draft ordinance. Ms. PÉREZ requested that staff present a Draft Historic
  Preservation Ordinance to the Historic Preservation Commission and proceed with community
  outreach, allow staff to work with any pending building applications on potentially historic sites
  and in the event that property owners are not receptive then Council could consider additional
  interim protection measures. Mayor MAZA and Ms. RINGHOFF discussed the process for
  identifying historic properties using the historic context survey. Mr. MAZA and Mr. HO
  discussed the public outreach process for the next public meetings, the role of the Historic
  Preservation Commission, and the notification process for homes on the survey. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER requested utilizing the Around Alhambra publication for outreach, which
  Mr. MONTES clarified that City funds could not be used for that and Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER
  clarified that perhaps staff could request an article from the Chamber about the community
  meetings.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed this informational report.

 CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 7 – 35)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No.19, 20, and 26, were

7.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: PURCHASE OF A NEW CNG COMPRESSOR FOR THE
  ALHAMBRA CITY YARD – F2M24-6B, N2M24-61

  The Alhambra City Yard is the main hub for fueling the Alhambra Community Transit buses,
  Public Works street sweepers, and other CNG fuel vehicles. Unfortunately, one of the older
  compressors recently experienced a catastrophic failure, leaving the staff heavily reliant on
  the remaining compressor to refuel the entire fleet. Staff sought to purchase and install a new
  compressor to alleviate the stress on the single unit, which was running longer hours than
  intended.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids for the
  purchase and delivery of a new compressed natural gas compressor; and, directed staff to
  undertake the necessary steps to finalize the Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  RESOLUTION: FY 2024-2025 PROJECT IDENTIFICATION FOR THE ROAD REPAIR AND
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017 (SB1 BEALL) – F2M24-45, R2M24-16

  The Road Repair and Accountability Act stipulated that, prior to receiving Road Maintenance
  and Rehabilitation Account (RMRA) funds in a fiscal year, a city or county must submit to the
  California Transportation Commission (CTC) a project list pursuant to an adopted resolution.
  This information would be due by July 1, 2024. Staff proposed a Street Rehabilitation Project
  for FY 2024-2025 that included design services and street rehabilitation (including but not
  limited to pavement, striping, ADA ramps, sidewalk, curb and gutter, etc.) for public streets
  bound by Valley Boulevard, Fremont Avenue, the I-10 freeway in the City of Alhambra and the
  West City Limit. It was anticipated that the City would receive $2,114,338.00 from the RMRA
  Fund for FY 2024-2025.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-16 entitled: A Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California adopting the fiscal year 2024-25 list of
  projects funded by SB 1: The Road Repair and Accountability Act; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, PÉREZ, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MAZA
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  AWARD CONTRACT: 2024 USDA SUMMER FOOD SERVICE PROGRAM – F2M24-25,
  N2M24-27, C2M24-30, M2M24-69

  On February 26, 2024, the City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids for
  the 2024 Summer Food Service Program. Staff included the following food vendors in the
  bidding process: Food Service Outreach, Inc., San Gabriel Unified School District, JA Food
  Service, School Nutrition Plus, Inc., and Unity Meals. On April 18, 2024, the City Clerk received
  two bids in the amount of $88,560.00 and $91,420.80. The bid received by School Nutrition
  Plus, Inc. was the lowest responsive bid.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and the City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and School
  Nutrition Plus, Inc., for the 2024 Summer Food Service Program in the amount of $88,560.00;

11.  CONTRACT APPROVAL: ALHAMBRA CENTRAL BUSINESS DISTRICT
  ASSOCIATION FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-2025 – F2M21-50, C2M24-31, M2M24-70

  Staff requested City Council approval of an agreement with the Alhambra Central Business
  District Association (ACBDA) for the 2024-2025 fiscal year. Since 1974 the City has
  maintained agreements with the ACBDA to provide promotional support to the merchants in
  the Central Business District of Alhambra. These merchants have an assessment placed upon
  them, in accordance with the Alhambra Municipal Code, Section 5.04.201, which is collected
  by the City and allocated for marketing and promotion activities specific to the District area.
  According to the City’s agreement with the ACBDA, a maximum of ninety percent (90%) of the
  total funds collected each year by the City may be allocated to the ACBDA.

  R2M24-17

  As part of the biennial review process and due to the fact that recent appointments made to
  the City’s Historic Preservation Commission have created a quorum for the Commission which

  COUNTY SANITATION DISTRICT NOS. 2 &16 OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY REQUIRED

  F2M24-46, R2M24-18

  On August 28, 2023, in accordance with Alhambra City Charter Sec. 29, the Alhambra City
  Council reorganized and rotated the offices of Mayor, Vice Mayor and Councilpersons of
  various departments for the nine-month period ending May 27, 2024. Adoption of a Resolution

  May 28, 2024, was the City’s Member; and, Katherine Lee was the Alternate Member to act in
  place of Ms. Pérez, if necessary.

14.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: INTERIOR COATINGS OF TREATMENT VESSELS 204 A AND
  204 B AT THE GROUND WATER TREATMENT PLANT – F2M24-47, N2M24-62

  The two water treatment Vessels 204 A and 204 B at the Ground Water Treatment Plant were
  not working due to the extent of the coating’s failure. It was determined that both vessels
  needed to be recoated. The Ground Water Treatment Facility has built in redundancy,
  therefore removing these vessels from service to complete the repairs would have no loss in
  production from the facility. Plans and specifications for the project were prepared; staff
  reviewed the plans, and found them to be consistent with the City’s standards.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Interior Coatings of Water Treatment Vessels 204 A and 204 B at
  the Ground Water Treatment Plant with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m. on May 30, 2024.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER

  City Manager BINNQUIST delivered a staff report. Staff requested that the City Council adopt a
  resolution to apply to Cal Fire’s Urban and Community Grant Program. This grant would fund
  crucial steps to advance the City’s management and improvement of its trees. As a part of this
  19
5-13-24
   grant the City would complete an updated inventory, a tree canopy assessment, the development
  of an Urban Forest Management Plan (UFMP), and tree planting. The UFMP would be the City’s
  guiding document to ensure that the benefits of a healthy urban forest are available to the
  community. A main goal of the UFMP would be to increase citywide canopy cover in order to
  maximize urban cooling, stormwater mitigation, air pollution mitigation, and improve walkability.
  After the UFMP was completed, the grant would fund a community tree planting campaign. This
  project would be applied for and completed in partnership with TreePeople. The objective of this
  grant would meet the goal of the 2024 Strategic Plan to promote sustainability.
